docs.title: xdfem2D
docs.text:
xdfem2D is a 2D finite-element structural analysis application — frames, walls, slabs and grillages — pairing a Python analysis library (xdfem2d) with a PySide6 desktop interface for building models, running analyses, and reviewing results interactively.

Units throughout are kN · m · kNm.

docs.title: Two domains, one model type
docs.text: Every model is either plane (a frame or wall in its own plane) or plate (a slab or grillage bending out of plane) — chosen once, in New model, and fixed for the model's life. The two share the same solver machinery but mean different things element by element: see Domains (plane vs plate) for the full comparison, then Plane models and Plate models for the elements, supports, loads and results of each.

docs.title: AI: assistant and agent
docs.text:
Two optional ways to work with a model by talking to it (see AI in xdfem2D):

  • The Assistant is a panel in the application that answers questions about the open model and makes edits. It runs local models by default (gemma4:e4b through Ollama), or a remote one with your own API key.
  • The Agent tab lets a coding agent (Claude Code, or Ollama's cloud models) build, analyse and design on the model you have open while you watch it change. The same tools are an MCP server for any agent you use.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
• Models. Frames, trusses, arches and walls (plane), and slabs and grillages (plate). Beams, membrane triangles and quads, plate-bending triangles and quads, and grillage members with torsion. Supports, springs (including tension-only and compression-only), multi-point constraints, and parametric geometry objects that are meshed when the model is solved. See Modelling, Plane models and Plate models.
  • Loads and analysis. Load cases, point, distributed, area, thermal and settlement loads, and self-weight. Linear, non-linear, mass, modal, response-spectrum (EC8) and, in plane models, P-Delta analysis; automatic EN 1990 combinations; variants and construction sequences. A load case is only a definition of loads, an analysis case is what gets solved, and a combination combines analysis cases: see Analysis.
  • Results and design. Displacements, reactions, diagrams, stresses and slab moments, section cuts. Reinforced concrete (EC2, with crack width and punching), steel (EC3) and timber (EC5) design. See Results and Design.
  • Interchange. Reports (PDF, Word, Excel), drawings, DXF, SAP2000, IFC and Robot, and a model as a Python script. See Exporting.
  • AI, optional. An Assistant that answers about the open model and edits it, an Agent that does a job of several steps on it, and an MCP server for other agents. Nothing is turned on until you use it.
  • Scripting. The calculation engine is a Python library you can use without the interface. See Scripting with the engine.
  • Templates to start a model in seconds, and scenes (saved working subsets of a model): see Templates and Scenes.

docs.title: Where to start
docs.text:
• Starting a new model? Read Domains (plane vs plate) first — it's the one choice you can't change later.
  • New here? Read Installation then Getting Started.
  • Want a tour of the windows and controls? See The Interface.
  • Building a model? See Modelling, then Plane models or Plate models, and Loads.
  • Running and reviewing analyses? See Analysis and Results.
  • Working with the AI Assistant or an agent? See AI in xdfem2D.
  • Writing models in code? See Scripting with the engine.

docs.title: The Agent tab
docs.text:
The Agent tab is the second tab of the AI panel (View ▸ AI panel, or F10; View ▸ Agent tab opens it directly). In it a program that works by itself, Claude Code, one of Ollama's cloud models or OpenCode, builds, changes, analyses and designs on the model you have open, with the same tools as the MCP server. You watch the drawing change as it goes, you can edit between its steps, and each of its changes is one step of Undo.

It is not the Assistant. The Assistant answers one request at a time, usually with a small model that runs on your computer. The Agent takes a request that needs several steps ("a three-storey frame, designed, with a report") and does the steps itself, with a capable model that is usually in the cloud.

docs.title: Using it
docs.text:
1. Choose the agent and the model.
  2. Write what you want and press Cmd+Enter (Ctrl+Enter elsewhere); Enter is a new line.
  3. The first time, the window tells you where your model goes (see below). Nothing is turned on until you send a message.
  4. Watch the drawing and the list of steps in the conversation. Stop interrupts it; New conversation starts afresh.

docs.title: The controls
docs.text: Agent The program that does the work: Claude Code, Ollama (cloud) or OpenCode. A name followed by (not tried) has not been tested for real. Model The model it uses: for Claude Code its own default, Sonnet, Opus or Haiku; for Ollama (cloud) the cloud models your Ollama has. Refresh reads the list again. Options What an agent that connects from outside needs: for Claude Code the connection, the token, the environment and the registration (see below). Greyed out for Ollama (cloud), which has nothing to set. The box and Send Write the request; Cmd+Enter sends. While the agent works, Send becomes Stop. New conversation Clears the conversation and what the agent remembers of it. The tab does it by itself when you create or open another model, because its memory of the old one would mislead it. ⓘ Opens this page in the application, with no internet needed. The line at the bottom Where the connection stands.

docs.title: The agents
docs.text:
Claude Code is run without a terminal (claude -p), given the server of the window in the request itself, so nothing has to be registered for the tab to work. It is closed in on the tools of the application: it has no shell and it cannot edit files. Options holds the connection: turn the server on or off, see the token, set the environment it runs in (KEY=VALUE lines, for example ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://localhost:11434 to use a model that runs on this computer), and Register with the agent, which runs claude mcp add for you so that Claude Code can also use the server outside the window.

OpenCode (opencode.ai) is a program like Claude Code that talks to many providers: its own free models, OpenAI, and a model that runs on this computer through Ollama. Install it and choose a model in it once; the Model list shows the ones it offers. It is run without a terminal and given the server of the window for that run only; everything else it could do (a shell, editing files) is refused. Where your model goes depends on the model you choose: a local one (ollama/…) stays on this computer, the others are sent to their provider, and the tab says which. OpenCode's own free models cost nothing, but each has the terms of its provider: some keep nothing and do not train on what you send, one keeps it for 30 days, some may use it to improve the model, and the Nemotron ones are for trial use only, not for personal or confidential data. The list notes it beside each name, the notice says it again, and the terms can change: see OpenCode's page. Do not use a free model on a confidential project. With Default in the model list OpenCode picks the model itself (its configuration, else the last one you used), so the tab cannot say where your model goes: choose a model to know.

Ollama (cloud) runs inside the application, for Ollama's cloud models only (gemma4:cloud, gpt-oss:120b-cloud …). It needs Ollama installed and signed in (ollama signin), and nothing else: no server, no token, no registration. Nothing runs on this computer, but every step is a request to Ollama's cloud and counts against your Ollama usage; the tab says how many calls a message took. If the quota is used up, or you are not signed in, it says so in those words. It keeps the last 40 messages of the conversation.

docs.title: Where your model goes
docs.text: Claude Code sends what you write and your model (nodes, loads, results) to Anthropic to answer, as it does in a terminal. Ollama (cloud) sends them to Ollama (ollama.com). The window says so once for each agent (with Don't show this again). With a model that runs on this computer it says that it stays here; small models often fail on requests of several steps. Do not use an agent on a project you may not share.

docs.title: What the agent can do in the window
docs.text:
• Build and change the model with the command language, including copying, arrays, rotations and mirrors, and the mass, modal, response-spectrum and P-Delta cases.
  • Analyse and design, and read the results; the window is locked on them as after a Run, and the design shows in the design views.
  • Show things: a view or a diagram (moment of the combination C1), the layers, the colours of the results, the grid, the zoom. A figure written to a file is a different request: it needs a path.
  • Select: a select marks bars and nodes in the drawing, so you see what it means.
  • Save and open files, lock the model so that nothing changes it, undo.

The tools are listed in The MCP server.

docs.title: What to know
docs.text:
• Turns, not a race. Each tool the agent calls reads the model as the window has it at that moment and writes its change back at the end. If you edit between two calls it sees it in the next one. If you edit during one, that call writes nothing and says so, and the agent repeats it from what it reads again.
  • Long calls keep the model still. While an analysis, a design or an export runs, the status bar shows Agent: working (...) and editing is switched off, as when the Variants panel is open. A short call does not take the model away.
  • Undo is yours. Each call that changes the model is one step of Edit ▸ Undo, together with your own. The status bar says what it did (Agent: +2 nodes, +1 bar).
  • Editing a solved model drops its results, whoever edits.
  • Selection. select adds to what is selected (as in a CAD program); select only replaces it, deselect takes from it, select none clears it and select previous goes back to the previous selection of the Selection menu. An action that uses the selection (move, divide, delete …) leaves nothing selected; select previous brings it back.
  • Files. What the agent saves goes to the folder of the open model, or to the default file location of Preferences when no model is open; nobody chooses it, it follows the model you open, and a path outside it is refused. A file it saves or opens becomes the one the window has open and joins File ▸ Open recent, as when you do it.
  • Safety. The server of the tab listens on this computer only (127.0.0.1) and answers only a client that sends the token. It turns off when you close the window, and it is never on unless you started it by sending a message.
  • Not shared. The zoom, the scenes and the variant you are looking at are yours; the agent works on the base model.

docs.title: If something does not work
docs.text: What you see Why Claude Code was not found on this computer (or OpenCode) It is not installed, or not on the path of the application. Install it, or start the application from a terminal where claude (or opencode) works. Sign in (Ollama cloud) Run ollama signin in a terminal. Limit reached (Ollama cloud) The free usage of the period is used up: wait, or use another agent. Claude Code says it cannot connect to xdfem2d-window A registration made earlier, in the folder you were in, has another port and wins there: run claude mcp remove xdfem2d-window -s local in that folder (claude mcp list shows both). The tab's own conversation does not use registrations. The agent asks for a path A figure or an export written to a file needs one; to see a view, ask it to show it. A model of Ollama is not in the list Only the cloud models are offered; Refresh reads the list again.

docs.title: AI in xdfem2D
docs.text:
xdfem2D has two ways of working with a model by talking to it. Both are in the AI panel at the left of the window (View ▸ AI panel, or F10), as two tabs:

  • the Assistant, which answers questions about the open model and makes the changes you ask for, one request at a time;
  • the Agent, which takes a request that needs several steps and does the steps itself, on the open model, while you watch.

Both are optional. Every other part of xdfem2D works without them, and nothing is turned on until you send a message.

docs.title: Which one to use
docs.text:
Assistant Agent What it is for A question or one change: which combination governs the reinforcement of E3?, add a 20 kN load at midspan, show the deformed shape. A job of several steps: a three-storey frame, designed to EC2, with a report. Who decides the steps You: one request, one answer. The agent: it plans, tries, reads the result and goes on. The model it uses Usually a small model that runs on your computer (through Ollama; gemma4:e4b to begin with), or a remote one with your own key. A capable model, usually in the cloud: Claude Code, Ollama's cloud models, or OpenCode (which can also use a model on your computer). What it can do Answer about the model and its results; build and change the model; do what the menus and the Display panel do; run the verifications of the Design menu; free conversation. Everything the Assistant does, and chain it: edit, analyse, design, read the results to decide the next step, make variants and construction sequences, seismic and second-order analyses, write reports and drawings, copy and mirror geometry. How you drive it A sentence, or a sentence with a prefix (?, +, =, >, :) that says what kind of request it is. A request in your own words. There are no prefixes. Speed Seconds. Tens of seconds to minutes. What leaves your computer Nothing with a local model. A remote model receives your question and a summary of the model. Your model, always: it is a remote model. Cost Free with a local model; a remote one uses your key. Claude Code uses your Claude plan; Ollama's cloud models use your Ollama usage.

Rule of thumb. Start with the Assistant: it is quick, it keeps your model on your computer, and for a question or a short edit it is enough. Turn to the Agent when the job has several steps that depend on each other, or when a small model keeps failing at it.

docs.title: What they share
docs.text:
• The same box and the same buttons. Write and press Cmd+Enter (Ctrl+Enter elsewhere); Enter is a new line. Send becomes Stop while an answer comes, New conversation starts afresh, and ⓘ opens the page of the tab, in the application.
  • Your model stays yours. What they do to it is one step of Undo (Ctrl+Z), and an edit to an analysed model drops its results, whoever makes it: run the analysis again.
  • Checked before it happens. The Assistant tries every change on a copy of the model first; the Agent's tools refuse what does not make sense and say why. Neither can run a program on your computer or write a file outside the folder of the open model.
  • They say where your model goes. Before a message goes to a remote model you are asked once, with Don't show this again (Preferences ▸ AI Assistant ▸ Show the assistant's warnings again brings it back).

docs.title: Other agents, outside the window
docs.text: The same tools are an MCP server (xdfem2D --mcp), so an agent you already use, such as Claude Code or Claude Desktop, can build and analyse a model of its own with xdfem2D as one more tool, with no window open. See The MCP server.

docs.title: Where to go next
docs.text:
• The AI Assistant: the kinds of request and how to say which, the model and its settings (temperature, Think), how good each model is.
  • The Agent tab: the agents, what each needs, what the agent can do in the window, and what to know.
  • The MCP server: registering it with another agent, the tools, the command language.

docs.title: Analysis
docs.text:
xdfem2D uses a three-tier model. Keeping these distinct is the key to using the program correctly.

Load case        Analysis case            Combination
──────────       ─────────────            ───────────
defines loads →  applies load cases   →   combines analysis cases
(no results)     with factors & a         (linear / envelope / SRSS / seismic)
                 solution method
                 (produces results)
  • Load case — a named set of loads. It is only a definition; on its own it produces no results.
  • Analysis case — references one or more load cases with factors and a solution method, and is solved. This is where results come from.
  • Combination — combines analysis cases (never load cases directly).

Automatic Linear cases

Adding a load case creates a Linear analysis case of the same name. If you build a combination that needs a load case directly, xdfem2D wraps that load case in a Linear analysis case automatically, so combinations always combine analysis cases.

docs.title: Analysis cases
docs.text:
Create them on the Analysis Cases sub-tab. Each type has its own form:

Type Purpose Key inputs Plane Plate Linear Static linear-elastic solution load-case coefficients; optional stored stiffness from a P-Delta run yes yes NonLinear Static solution honouring unilateral (tension-/compression-only) springs load-case coefficients (same inputs as Linear) yes yes Mass Build a mass matrix from gravity loads and/or nodal masses load-case→mass factors (e.g. G + 0.3·Q); concentrated nodal masses yes yes Modal Eigenvalue analysis number of modes; the Mass case to use yes (in-plane modes) yes (vertical modes) Spectrum Response-spectrum analysis Modal case; spectral function; combination rule (SRSS/CQC); direction; damping yes (X, Y or XY) yes (vertical) Geometric Nonlinear P-Delta / large displacement method; max iterations; tolerance; member stiffness factors; load-case coefficients yes no Sequence Incremental staged-construction analysis defined by a construction sequence (see Variants & Construction Sequences); appears automatically when a sequence is created yes yes

P-Delta is not available in a plate model: its geometric stiffness is built from in-plane axial force, which a plate model does not carry. Everything else is available in both domains. What changes with the domain is where the mass sits and what a mode is, as the Mass and Modal section shows side by side.

A Linear case may reuse the tangent stiffness of a Geometric Nonlinear (P-Delta) run instead of the elastic stiffness.

docs.title: NonLinear cases (unilateral springs)
docs.text:
A NonLinear case takes exactly the same inputs as a Linear case (load-case coefficients) but solves the model honouring tension-only / compression-only springs — see Springs. It is the only case type that activates that unilateral behaviour; in every other case type a spring acts bilaterally (resisting in both directions).

How it is solved: the case builds the combined load vector (Σ coeffᵢ · load caseᵢ) and runs an active-set iteration — each unilateral spring is included in the stiffness only while it is active (its displacement has the sign matching its mode), re-solving until the active set no longer changes. Because the result is non-linear, it cannot be scaled or superposed, which drives the combination rule below.

When a NonLinear case behaves like Linear

If the model has no tension-/compression-only springs, a NonLinear case produces exactly the same result as a Linear case.

docs.title: Mass and Modal cases
docs.text:
The mass matrix is diagonal (lumped). What it holds, and what a mode is, depends on the domain:

Plane Plate Mass from a load case the absolute vertical force \|Fy\|/g at each node, placed equally on ux and uy the absolute transverse force \|Fz\|/g, placed on w only Concentrated nodal mass Mx on ux, My on uy, Mtz rotational inertia Mx on w; My, Mtz rotational inertias about x and y Rotary inertia none unless Mtz is given none unless My / Mtz are given A mode is an in-plane vibration an out-of-plane (vertical) vibration Directions X and Y one, vertical

In a plane model this has two consequences worth knowing before reading modal results:

  • an upward load contributes the same mass as a downward one, and a purely horizontal load contributes no mass at all;
  • there is no rotary inertia unless a rotational nodal mass (mtz) is given explicitly.

Rocking modes need an explicit rotary inertia

Degrees of freedom with no mass (typically the nodal rotations; in a plate model θx and θy) are eliminated exactly by static condensation, so they cost no accuracy and produce no spurious modes. But a mode whose kinematics involve those rotations — the rocking of a rigid block on springs is the typical case — only exists if it has a rotational mass mtz: without it the rocking merges with heave. For a member lumped into segments of length h, the consistent value is mtz = mᵢ·h²/12 at each node.

Effective mass percentages are relative to the FREE mass

meff X % and meff Y % (in a plate model only the one, vertical, direction) use as denominator the mass on the unrestrained degrees of freedom, reported as total_mass_x / total_mass_y. Mass lumped on a restrained DOF cannot vibrate — it goes straight to the foundation — so it is excluded. The denominator is chosen so that the percentages of all modes add up to 100 %, which makes the column a reliable indicator of mode truncation.

This is not the model's total mass. The results also carry model_mass_x / model_mass_y (everything, restrained included) and restrained_mass_x / restrained_mass_y, so the ratio against the total can be computed when needed — notably for the EC8 §4.3.3.3.1 criterion, which asks for 90 % of the total mass of the structure.

How much is excluded depends on the mesh, not on the structure: on a simply supported beam discretised into n elements the supported nodes carry exactly 1/n of the mass (6,3 % with 16 elements). Refining the mesh therefore moves the percentages even though the absolute effective masses converge. When the restrained fraction exceeds 2 %, the Modal case results include a warnings entry saying so.

Model check (Structure menu) additionally reports any concentrated nodal mass placed on a restrained DOF, since that is almost always a modelling slip rather than an intention.

docs.title: Response spectra (seismic)
docs.text:
A Spectrum analysis case reads a spectral function — a curve of spectral acceleration Sa(T) — and a referenced Modal case, then combines the modal responses (SRSS or CQC) in a chosen direction: X, Y or XY in a plane model; in a plate model the one, vertical, direction. Define the spectral functions in Structure → Spectral Functions. You can build one three ways:

  • By code (EC8:2004) — pick Type 1 / Type 2, ground type A–E, the reference ground acceleration agR, importance factor γI and damping ξ. Choose Design (Sd) — which uses the behaviour factor q and the lower-bound factor β — or Elastic (Se). The soil parameters (S, TB, TC, TD) are derived and shown.
  • By national-annex zone — the same, driven by a seismicity zone that fixes agR.
  • User-defined — enter S, TB, TC, TD and ag directly, or a raw list of (T, Sa) points.

The response-spectrum result of a Spectrum case is the peak (absolute) response; when it enters a combination it becomes a seismic envelope (see below).

docs.title: Combinations
docs.text:
Create them on the Combinations sub-tab. A combination references analysis cases only — eligible members are Linear, NonLinear, P-Delta (Geometric Nonlinear, plane only), and Spectrum cases. Modal and Mass cases cannot be combined.

NonLinear cases in combinations

A non-linear result cannot be scaled or added to others, so a combination that references a NonLinear case may contain only that single case, with a combination factor of 1.0 — no other analysis cases of any type. xdfem2D rejects combinations that break this rule.

Combination types:

Type Rule LinearSum Σ coeffᵢ · caseᵢ (signed linear superposition) Envelope Envelope: max/min of each component across the weighted cases AbsSum Σ |coeffᵢ · caseᵢ| (sum of absolutes) SRSS √(Σ (coeffᵢ · caseᵢ)²) (SRSS)

When a combination references a Spectrum case, the result becomes a seismic envelope: the gravity base ± Σ |coeffₛ · spectrumₛ|.

docs.title: Automatic Eurocode combinations
docs.text: Analysis → Auto Comb. (EN1990)… (Ctrl+Shift+C) generates ULS/SLS combinations from the load cases' action types. Generated combinations are folded into analysis-case references on the next refresh.

docs.title: Construction sequences
docs.text:
A Sequence analysis case represents an incremental staged-construction analysis. Each sequence is composed of ordered phases — each phase adds elements, applies load cases as an increment, and optionally changes the provisional support set. The solver carries locked-in forces forward from phase to phase, so later members do not attract load that earlier ones already resisted.

Sequence cases are created and edited in Analysis → Construction Sequences…. They appear in the case drop-down alongside normal cases and combinations (order: analysis cases → sequences → combinations), and their results are navigated phase by phase using the phase selector in the toolbar. See Variants & Construction Sequences for the full workflow.

docs.title: Running
docs.text: Press F5 or the Run button. Results lock the model; unlock with Ctrl+L to edit (which clears results). See Results.

docs.title: The AI Assistant
docs.text:
The Assistant tab of the AI panel answers questions about the open model in plain language (where the largest stress is, which combination governs the reinforcement, what a command does), makes the changes you ask for, and presses the buttons of the window for you. Show or hide the panel from View → AI panel.

It is optional. Every other part of xdfem2D works without it, and the panel says so when nothing is installed. For a job of several steps, the Agent tab does the steps itself; AI in xdfem2D compares the two.

docs.title: What you write decides what happens
docs.text:
You can just write. The assistant reads the sentence and decides which of five things you mean (this is Auto, and it is how it always starts). When you want to decide yourself, or it chose wrong, begin the sentence with a prefix.

Prefix Or Mode What it does Asks the model ? /q /query Query Answers a question about the open model and its results: which combination governs the reinforcement of E3? It reads; it never changes the model. First it tries a short typed question (get) that the program answers itself, exact and fast; if that is not enough, the model reads through its tools. yes + /c /create Create Builds or changes the model: add a 20 kN load at midspan. The model writes short commands that the application checks on a copy; if the commands cannot say it, a Python script, also checked on a copy. Applied at once or held for Apply (see Creating and changing a model). yes = /v /verify (or /check) Check Runs a verification of the members, as the Design menu does: concrete beams and columns, crack width, slabs and walls, steel, timber, and the suggested column reinforcement. The result shows in the design views. The analysis has to have been run. no > /a /action Action Does what a menu or the Display panel does: show the deformed shape, grid of 0.5 m, run the analysis, save as beam1 (see Doing what the window does). If it is not sure which action you mean it lists the closest and runs nothing. no : /i /assistant Assistant Free conversation: about the program, the manual, engineering in general. It does not see your model, so it is not for the numbers of your project. yes

"Asks the model" says whether the language model is used at all. Check and Action are carried out by the application itself: they are fast and cost nothing, even with a remote model selected.

docs.title: How a prefix is read
docs.text:
• Only at the very start of the sentence, and it is taken off before the sentence goes on.
  • A symbol counts only when a space or a letter follows it: +5 kN, =2 m and >=9 are numbers, not prefixes. A slash word counts only when it is the whole first word (/q which bar, not /quantity).
  • Type / in the box and the list of the kinds of request opens (pick one with the mouse, or with the arrows and Tab or Enter). As soon as a prefix is typed, the line under the box says what it does.

docs.title: With no prefix (Auto)
docs.text:
• A sentence with a question mark is a Query.
  • A sentence that only selects (select E2, select the beams at y=6, deselect V1, seleciona os nós A e B) is done at once, with no model: it marks them in the drawing and adds them to what is selected (select only ... replaces the selection, select none clears it, select previous goes back). An action that uses the selection (move, divide, delete …) leaves nothing selected; select previous brings it back.
  • Anything else the router decides between the five modes. When it is close, the answer says so.

docs.title: Which to use
docs.text: Write normally first. A prefix is for when you know better than the router, or for a short sentence that could be read two ways (+ 3 m is a change; 3 m? is a question). If an answer came from the wrong mode, repeat the sentence with the prefix you meant.

docs.title: Getting started
docs.text:
The Assistant ships without a language model. To use it:

  1. Install Ollama and start it (ollama serve; the Ollama desktop app does this for you).
  2. Fetch a model: ollama pull gemma4:e4b, about 9.5 GB. It is the one the assistant starts with (see Tested models); whichever you use must support tool calls.
  3. Open the panel (View ▸ AI panel, or F10) and press Refresh. The model appears in the list.
  4. Ask something, such as which supports does this model have?. If an answer comes, it works.

No Ollama, or a computer too slow for it? Use a remote service with an API key instead; see Where the model runs. A model is missing from the list? Refresh reads it again; a model marked — no tool support cannot be used. Without any of this, the rest of xdfem2D works exactly the same.

docs.title: The panel, from top to bottom
docs.text:
Provider and Providers…: where the assistant runs. Ollama (local) is your own machine; the others are services you have a key for. Providers… adds a key (see Where the model runs).

Model and Refresh: the models the provider offers; Refresh reads the list again. A note beside a name matters: — no tool support means the model cannot call the tools that read your model, so it would answer from nothing (do not use it); (ollama cloud) means it runs on Ollama's machines, so your model is sent there.

Temperature and Think: how the model answers. The defaults suit modelling; see Temperature and Think before changing them.

ⓘ: opens this page in the application, with no internet needed.

The box, Send and New conversation: write a request and press Cmd+Enter (Ctrl+Enter elsewhere); Enter is a new line. While an answer is coming Send becomes Stop. New conversation clears the conversation and what the model remembers of it.

Open and Apply: for a reply that wrote Python, or commands that are waiting. Apply applies them after checking again against the model that is open now; Open shows the Python in the script editor. They are greyed out when there is nothing to apply.

The router bar (at the bottom): how Auto decides. off is a plain keyword classifier; regression is the classifier of the application; regression + a model lets a model of embeddings help to choose the action of the window. Under each sentence it shows the mode it chose and how sure it was. (Confirming or correcting its choice is a developer tool: it shows only with router_verdicts = on under [assistant] in ~/.xdfem2d/config.ini.)

docs.title: What lasts and what is remembered
docs.text: The model, temperature and Think you choose in the panel last until you close the application. Preferences ▸ AI Assistant holds what it starts with, and changing a value there replaces the choice of the session (see Preferences). Also there: Apply the assistant's commands at once and Answer a request in one reply.

docs.title: Warnings
docs.text: Before a message goes to a remote model, and when you turn Think on, the assistant asks first. Each has Don't show this again; Preferences ▸ AI Assistant ▸ Show the assistant's warnings again brings them back. Checking every change on a copy of the model, and the notes under the replies, are always on.

docs.title: Temperature and Think
docs.text:
Two controls under the model list change how the model answers. The defaults are right for modelling: change them only for a reason.

Temperature (default 0) is how much the answer varies. A model writes an answer one word at a time, and at each step it has a ranked list of words that could come next. At temperature 0 it always takes the first of the list, so the same question gives the same answer. As the temperature rises it more and more often takes a lower one: the answers become more varied, and less careful.

  • 0: use it for modelling, for numbers and for anything the assistant has to do. A tool call is an exact format (a node id, a number, a name), so it shouldn't be neessary to be creative.
  • 0.1 to 0.2: for some hard question to which the model has answered wrong.
  • 0.3 to 0.7: only for free conversation, or to ask for alternatives (give me three layouts). The price is more wrong ids and invented values.
  • Above that the model starts to ramble, and a small model stops following the format of its tools.
  • It does not make a model smarter. If an answer is wrong at 0, a higher value is not the fix: ask again with more detail, or use a better model (see Choosing a model).

Think (default off) lets the model reason silently before it answers.

A reasoning pass costs time, and on a small model it is not necessarily better. Turning Think on shows a warning once (Don't show this again silences it), and it only acts on Ollama models. Below is a small guide to when it is worth trying.

Situation Try A short request, or a small model: you want the answer fast Think off (the default) A hard question (which combination governs?) is answered wrongly Think on The box is greyed out The model has no thinking channel: there is nothing to switch

Both last until you close the application. Preferences ▸ AI Assistant sets what a launch starts with.

docs.title: Where the model runs
docs.text:
The Provider at the top of the panel decides where the language model runs.

On your computer On another machine of yours A remote service Provider Ollama (local) Ollama (local), with OLLAMA_HOST OpenAI, Google Gemini, Ollama Cloud, … What leaves your network Nothing Nothing Your question, and what the assistant reads of your model Needs Ollama Ollama running on that machine An API key Quality and speed What your computer allows; a small model gives wrong answers that look right (see Choosing a model) A real GPU, with the same privacy The most reliable, and far better at building a model

Rule of thumb. Start local. Use a remote model when your computer is too slow, or when a model has to be built from a long description, and your work allows it. Under a confidentiality obligation, stay on your computer or on a machine of your own network: that is the speed of a real GPU with none of the disclosure.

A remote model receives the geometry, loads, sections and results the assistant reads to answer. The panel asks once per session before the first remote question (see Warnings).

docs.title: Using a remote service
docs.text: Press Providers… beside the model list, paste the key, and the service's models appear below a separator, labelled with the provider.

docs.title: Which services
docs.text:
Most services speak OpenAI's API at a different address, so OpenAI, Google Gemini, Ollama Cloud, DeepSeek, Kimi (Moonshot), GLM (Zhipu), Mistral, Groq and OpenRouter are already listed under Providers…. Paste a key beside one and its models join the list.

Anthropic is not among them: its API is shaped differently enough to need a second client library and a second translation of every tool, which is a lot of machinery — and a lot of megabytes in the packaged application — for one provider out of ten. Claude models are available through OpenRouter.

docs.title: Ollama in the cloud, or on another machine
docs.text:
Two different things, and only one of them sends your model away.

Ollama Cloud runs the models on Ollama's machines. Add an OLLAMA_API_KEY under Providers… and it behaves like any other remote service — same warning, same marking in the list. Useful on a laptop that cannot hold an 8B model.

Your own Ollama on another machine — an office workstation with a GPU, say — needs nothing here at all. The local provider follows Ollama's own OLLAMA_HOST variable:

export OLLAMA_HOST=http://workstation.local:11434

The panel then lists that machine's models and nothing leaves your network. For work under a confidentiality obligation this is the arrangement to prefer: the speed of a real GPU with none of the disclosure.

For anything else — a service newer than this release, or a company gateway — use Add endpoint… in the same dialog. It asks for a name and the base URL of the OpenAI-compatible API, and writes them to ~/.xdfem2d/llm_endpoints.json:

{
  "myprovider": {
    "env": "MYPROVIDER_API_KEY",
    "base_url": "https://api.example.com/v1",
    "models": ["some-model"]
  }
}

That file holds addresses, not secrets. An entry there overrides a built-in one, which is how to correct an address that has moved without waiting for a new release.

docs.title: Where the keys are kept
docs.text:
In your system keychain — Keychain Access on macOS, and the equivalent elsewhere — under the service name xdfem2d. They are encrypted at rest, and you can inspect or revoke them there without going through this application.

They are never written to the preferences file, which is plain text, and never into a .x2d, which would carry the key to whoever you send the model to.

An environment variable of the same name still works and is useful for scripting, but it is second in line: a key stored through the dialog wins. Note that launching from the Dock or Finder does not inherit shell variables, so a key set only in ~/.zshrc will appear missing — another reason to prefer the dialog.

Storing keys needs the keyring package, which ships with xdfem2D. It is not a vault of its own — on macOS it is a thin layer over the system Keychain, the same one Safari uses, and the entries appear in Keychain Access under the service name xdfem2d. The first time a key is saved, macOS asks whether Python may use the Keychain; answer Always Allow or it will ask again at every start.

If it is missing from your environment, install it with pip install keyring. The dialog says so rather than failing quietly, and falls back to environment variables meanwhile.

No extra install is needed for any of them. The openai client is a normal dependency of xdfem2D and ships with the packaged application, and every provider above is reached through it — only the key is missing.

docs.title: Choosing a model
docs.text:
The model, temperature and Think you choose in the panel are for the current session; the ones in Preferences ▸ AI Assistant are what a launch starts with (see The panel).

Two things matter, and neither is obvious from the model's name.

It must support tool calling. The assistant never guesses: it asks the application for the numbers through a set of query tools. A model that cannot call them will answer anyway, from nothing, and the invented stresses look exactly like real ones. The panel marks such models — no tool support.

Bigger is not a luxury here. This is the part worth reading twice. A smaller model answers faster and fits in less memory, so it looks like the sensible choice on a modest machine. It is not. In testing, a 3B model asked to locate the most stressed element named the right element, skipped the tool that knows where it is, and reported fabricated coordinates — adding that they were "derived from the element locations within the analysed mesh", which they were not. It did this in two runs out of five. The same model described required reinforcement as "the limit you must not exceed", inverting the meaning while quoting the correct figure.

A small model here does not give worse answers. It gives wrong answers that look exactly like right ones.

docs.title: Tested models
docs.text:
The Assistant writes short commands (the command language, one request at a time) that the application checks and applies. Three benchmarks measure it (in tools/bench/), all at temperature 0, with the thinking of the model off and the router off, in October 2026. A request is right when the model it leaves passes a check made for that request, or when the answer to a question has the value asked:

  • Create (bench_create.py): 86 requests that build or change a model (nodes and bars, supports, loads, sections and materials, load cases and combinations, editing and deleting, hinges, links and springs, slabs and walls, and the dynamic cases: mass, modal, response spectrum, P-Delta, non-linear).
  • Query (bench_query.py): 90 questions about a model that was analysed (counts, reactions, displacements, forces, geometry, design, combinations).
  • Chain (bench_scenarios.py, scenario S1): 36 sentences, in three chains of 12 steps (a wall with edge supports and loads, then mass, modal, spectrum and combinations), in which each step is worded at random in one of three ways and works on the model that the previous steps left.
Model Create Query Chain Time per request Notes gemma4:e4b 73/86 84/90 24/36 about 1 s The default. The fastest of the local models, and the one that falls behind most on the chain. bonsai-2:27b 74/86 87/90 34/36 about 5 to 7 s The most capable of the local models, and the slowest. gemma4:cloud 84/86 85/90 36/36 under 1 s Ollama's cloud model: the best result on the chain, but your model leaves this computer. beam:cloud 84/86 89/90 32/36 about 1 s A larger cloud model, with the best result on questions.

Where the small models fail is the same everywhere: a request that leaves something to guess (the top-left corner, the centre), a request of several steps, and an id that does not exist yet. In the chain, gemma4:e4b misses the same steps in every run: the wall read from 4,0x20,0 m2 em (6,0), the loads and supports on an edge, and the nodal load. The wording matters: when the same requests were asked again with a trivial change (a full stop, please, Portuguese instead of English), gemma4:e4b lost between 6 and 14 points. Earlier tests with other, smaller models (3 to 4 B, such as qwen3.5:4b, ministral-3:3b and granite4.2:3b) with another set of requests gave much worse results, and they were not measured again.

Times are from one machine (an Apple-silicon Mac). Without a usable GPU the same model can be several times slower, and the cloud time depends on your connection. Results move by one or two requests between runs.

These names will age. You can use any other models that support tool calling.

docs.title: A tool call that comes back as text
docs.text:
Occasionally a model — even one that generally supports tool calling — writes what looks like a tool call as plain text instead of actually making one: something like {"tool_calls": [...]} appears as the answer itself. The panel cannot act on that; it is not a real call, and the reply is marked "answered without consulting the model — treat any numbers as unverified".

This is not the application failing to recognise a valid call — it is the underlying runtime (Ollama) failing to recognise the model's output as one, because the model drifted slightly off the exact format its own chat template expects. It tends to happen more with smaller models, and not always on the same question twice.

The Temperature control is the knob for this. Lower keeps the model closer to the format it was trained to reproduce exactly: steadier tool use, less varied wording. The default is already 0. It does not make the drift impossible, only less likely; a model with no tool support at all will not gain any by turning this down.

docs.title: What it can and cannot do
docs.text:
It reads, and it can build and change the model. It builds a structure from a description and makes changes to the open model — add, edit, delete, assign — checked on a copy first (see Creating and changing a model). What the model itself cannot do is run the analysis or write a file: that is for the Action mode, which presses the button of the window (> run the analysis, > write the report) and is carried out by the application, not by the model. For several steps in a row, with the results read in between, use the Agent.

It is given a short summary of the model up front and asks for detail through the tools, so it sees the geometry, loads, cases, results, nodal-averaged stresses, design results, constraints and this manual. Results are keyed to the analysed mesh — the elements that geometry objects expand into — and the assistant uses those ids, which is why they may not match what you drew.

docs.title: Doing what the window does
docs.text:
This is the Action mode (>). Some requests are not about the model but about the window: "show the deformed shape", "hide the node labels", "put the grid at 50 cm", "use the plasma colormap", "save as beam1". The assistant recognises them (in Portuguese, English or French) and runs the menu command or the Display panel control itself, then says what it did. This covers the File, Edit, View, Selection, Analysis and Design menus and the Display panel: its layers, the grid (spacing, snap, reference lines) and the Style tab (colormap, smoothing, fill, levels, contour lines, scale, diagram and utilisation styles). A number or a name in the sentence is read ("grelha de 50 cm", "15 níveis", "paleta plasma"). A command that deletes or replaces something asks first, and one that is greyed out says why: a Style control waits for a view that has a colour map, a diagram or a design to style, and says which view to open.

An agent (the Agent tab of the same panel) can do the display part too, and much more: see The Agent tab.

docs.title: Creating and changing a model
docs.text:
Ask in plain language — "a 6 m simply supported beam", "a cantilever wall", "add a 20 kN load at midspan", "give bar B1 the section S2". Ask for one thing at a time: small models do each request well and a long list badly. The assistant answers in one of two ways, and the note under the reply says which:

  • Commands. Four verbs (add, set, remove, move) are what it tries first; a block is all or nothing — if one line fails, none is applied. They are checked on a copy of the model, and if they are valid they are applied to the open model at once (Ctrl+Z undoes; the results are discarded, so run the analysis again). A block of more than 10 lines, or one that removes three or more elements, waits for the Apply button instead, and the note says why.
  • Python. When the commands cannot say it, it writes Python for the model that is open (plain model.… calls, using the xdfem2d API). It is run on a copy first, and if it runs and checks out it is applied at once, exactly like the commands. The line count does not matter for Python (a script is long by nature); only what it removes does. It waits for Apply when the model is locked, when it places a template over a model that already has geometry (Apply then asks whether to insert the template or replace the model), when it does not run on the model that is open now, or when it removes three or more elements.

In both cases Apply applies what waits, after checking it again against the model open at that moment, and Open shows the Python in the Script editor (Ctrl+Shift+E), where you can read or fix it; Open also works after the Python was applied. Nothing runs from the editor until you press Run yourself. Preferences ▸ AI Assistant ▸ Apply the assistant's commands at once switches the automatic application off, so that everything waits for Apply.

This is genuinely useful for a quick starting point and for routine edits, but treat it as early and limited:

  • the more elaborate the request, the more likely something is missing or wrong, so review what was applied before you build on it;
  • a capable model matters most here. A small local model often produces a structure that looks right and is not; a stronger remote model (with an API key) is markedly better both at answering and at building.

Two habits make it more useful:

  • Name the case. "In COMBO1" rather than "in the model": extremes differ between load cases and combinations, and the assistant will otherwise have to pick one and tell you which.
  • Check anything that matters. Use Edit → Find Entity to jump to an element it names, and confirm the number in the results table. The assistant is a way to find things quickly, not a substitute for reading the results.

Design values exist only for combinations that were actually designed. Ask about an analysis case and a good model will tell you there is nothing there.

docs.title: Command Language
docs.text:
The command language is a short text for building and changing a model, one command per line, without Python. The Assistant writes it when you ask it to create or change something, and an agent working through the MCP server writes it to edit your model. When the Assistant holds its commands for Apply, what you read there is this language, and this page says what each line means.

add section S1 concrete 0.3x0.5
add node A 0 0
add node B 6 0
add bar E1 A B S1
add support pin A
add support roller B
add load 15 down on E1 case Q
set bar E1 section S2
remove load on E1

docs.title: How a line is built
docs.text:
VERB OBJECT [ID] [SELECTOR] [properties]
  • There are a few verbs, applied to the same objects: add creates, set changes, remove deletes, move moves nodes. The same words build a model and change one that exists.
  • Units are metres, kN, kNm and degrees. x is horizontal and y is up.
  • An id is a name: you choose it when you add something, and it is the one the model shows for anything that exists.
  • # starts a comment, and blank lines are ignored.
  • add of a name that exists is an error. set and remove of one that does not exist is an error that lists the ones that do.
  • A load names its case (case Q). The case is made, as a permanent action, when it is new.

docs.title: Selectors
docs.text:
Where a command takes an id it also takes a selector, which picks several things at once:

Selector Picks N1, N1,N3 those ids nodes all, bars all everything of that kind nodes x=0.5, nodes y<2, nodes x>=3 and y=0 nodes by their coordinates bars section=B1, bars material=X bars by their section or material nodes supported, nodes free nodes with or without a support

An empty selection is an error that says what exists (no node with x=0.5; x of the nodes: 0, 2, 4). It is never a command that quietly does nothing.

docs.title: All or nothing
docs.text: The commands run on a copy of the model, and the copy replaces the model only if every line worked. On an error nothing changes and the message says the line and why. This is what makes it safe to let a model, or an agent, write them: what you see before accepting is what is applied.

docs.title: Notation in the list
docs.text:
In the list below, words in capitals are what you write (ID, SEL, X Y), [ ] is optional, | is "one of", and what follows e.g. is a line that works. The text in parentheses explains the form.

The Assistant is taught only the forms most requests need, because a small model writes them better when it has fewer to choose from. The rest (the dynamic analyses, the Edit-menu operations and the reading commands for design, quantities and the model check) are for agents, and the interpreter accepts them all.

docs.title: add
docs.text:
Creates something new: nodes, bars, sections, supports, loads, cases, combinations, analyses, constraints. An add of a name that already exists is an error.

add node ID X Y
    e.g. add node A 0 0
add bar ID NODE NODE SECTION [hinge-start] [hinge-end]
    e.g. add bar E1 A B S1
add section NAME concrete BxH [CLASS] | steel PROFILE [GRADE] | timber BxH [CLASS]
    e.g. add section S1 concrete 0.3x0.5
add material NAME steel GRADE | concrete CLASS [REBAR] | timber CLASS | young E [poisson V] [weight V]   (the last one is a generic material of your own numbers, E as 30GPa, weight in kN/m3)
    e.g. add material X steel S355
    e.g. add material M young 20GPa poisson 0.25 weight 20
add slab ID X0 Y0 X1 Y1 thickness T [material M]
add slab ID thickness T [material M] points X Y X Y X Y ...
add slab ID regular sides N diameter D thickness T [material M] [center X Y]
add slab ID nodes N1 N2 [N3 ...] [section NAME]   (corners are existing nodes: 2 = rectangle, 3+ = polygon)
    e.g. add slab S1 0 0 5 4 thickness 0.2
    e.g. add slab S2 nodes A B C
add wall ID X0 Y0 X1 Y1 thickness T [material M]
    e.g. add wall W1 0 0 4 3 thickness 0.25
add support fix|pin|roller SEL [free x|y]
SEL: ids (A,D) or a condition (nodes x=0.5, nodes y=0, nodes all)
    e.g. add support fix A,D
add spring SEL [kx V] [ky V] [kt V]   (kN/m, kNm/rad; write the name of each stiffness)
    e.g. add spring B ky 2000
add spring on bars SEL [kx V] [ky V]   (a distributed spring, kN/m per metre of bar; kx axial, ky transverse to the bar)
    e.g. add spring on bars E1,E2 ky 5000
add spring on slab SEL kz V   (a Winkler spring under a slab or wall, kN/m3)
    e.g. add spring on slab Slab kz 20000
add edge REGION EDGE KIND   (EDGE 0, 1, ... or bottom|right|top|left|all; KIND pin|fix|roller-x|roller-y|symm-x|symm-y)
    e.g. add edge Slab 1 pin
add case NAME [permanent|live|wind|seismic|temperature]
    e.g. add case Q live
add selfweight CASE [factor F]
    e.g. add selfweight G
add load VALUE [down|up|left|right] on SEL [at FRACTION] [case NAME]   (kN on a node or at a point of a bar, kN/m on a bar, kN/m2 on a slab; VALUE..VALUE is a trapezoid on a bar)
    e.g. add load 15 down on E1 case Q
add load VALUE [perp|tang|right|left|up|down] on edge REGION EDGE [case NAME]   (kN/m along one edge of a slab or wall; perp is normal to the edge, tang along it; right, left, up and down are along the global axes)
    e.g. add load 10 perp on edge Slab 1 case Q
add temperature uniform V [gradient V] on SEL [case NAME]
    e.g. add temperature uniform 30 on E1 case T
add settlement uy V [ux V] [tz V] on SEL [case NAME]   (uy negative is down, in metres)
    e.g. add settlement uy -0.01 on B case S
add analysis NAME = FACTOR CASE + FACTOR CASE ...   (load cases)
    e.g. add analysis ULS = 1.35 G + 1.5 Q
add analysis NAME mass = FACTOR CASE + ...   (the mass of the loads, kN / 9.81, for the modal case)
    e.g. add analysis M mass = 1 G + 0.3 Q
add analysis NAME modal mass MASSCASE [modes N]   (the vibration modes: read them with get modal)
    e.g. add analysis Modes modal mass M modes 6
add analysis NAME spectrum modal MODALCASE function SPECTRUM [direction X|Y|XY] [rule SRSS|CQC] [damping D]   (the response spectrum analysis)
    e.g. add analysis Sx spectrum modal Modes function EC8 direction X rule CQC
add analysis NAME pdelta = FACTOR CASE + ... [iterations N] [tolerance T] [beams F] [columns F]   (second order, plane domain; F is the fraction of the stiffness kept)
    e.g. add analysis P pdelta = 1.35 G + 1.5 Q beams 0.8 columns 0.8
add analysis NAME nonlinear = FACTOR CASE + ...   (unilateral springs)
add spectrum ID points T SA T SA ... [damping D]  |  add spectrum ID ec8 ag A S S TB T TC T TD T [damping PERCENT] [q Q [beta B]] [tmax T]  |  add spectrum ID predefined CODE SOIL ZONE [importance i|ii|iii|iv] [damping PERCENT] [q Q [beta B]] [tmax T]   (the response spectrum Sa(T); ec8: the EN 1998-1 curve, ag in m/s2, elastic or, with q, design; predefined: the parameters of CEN-1, CEN-2 (zone .1g ... .9g), PT-1 (zone 1.1 ... 1.6) or PT-2 (zone 2.1 ... 2.5), ground type A to E)
    e.g. add spectrum EC8 ec8 ag 1.5 S 1.2 TB 0.15 TC 0.5 TD 2
    e.g. add spectrum PT predefined PT-1 B 1.3 importance ii q 1.5
add mass SEL [mx V] [my V] [mtz V] case MASSCASE   (a concentrated mass, tonnes and t m2, for a Mass case)
    e.g. add analysis M mass = 1 G
    e.g. add mass B mx 2 my 2 case M
add combination NAME = FACTOR CASE + FACTOR CASE ...   (load or analysis cases)
    e.g. add combination C1 = 1.35 G + 1.5 Q
add combination NAME = FACTOR CASE + ... type sum|envelope|abssum|srss|nonlinear   (envelope: the largest and the smallest of each result over the terms; abssum: the sum of the absolute values; srss: the square root of the sum of squares; nonlinear: the combination of one non-linear analysis case, factor 1; sum is the default)
    e.g. add combination ENV = 1 ULS1 + 1 ULS2 type envelope
    e.g. add combination CNL = 1 NL type nonlinear
add constraint equal SEL COMPONENTS   (the nodes move together in these components: ux uy tz)
add constraint rigid MASTER SLAVES   (the slaves follow the master as one rigid body; the master is a node, the slaves are nodes or a condition)
add constraint equation 1*A.ux -1*B.ux = 0   (the raw form)
    e.g. add constraint equal B,C ux
    e.g. add constraint rigid A B,C

docs.title: set
docs.text:
Changes something that exists. Several attribute value pairs can go in one line.

set slab ID mesh S | thickness T | material M   (several pairs in one line; mesh is the size of the elements)
    e.g. set slab Slab mesh 0.25
set wall ID mesh S | thickness T | material M
    e.g. set wall W1 thickness 0.3
set bar SEL section NAME | hinge-start on|off | hinge-end on|off   (several pairs in one line)
    e.g. set bar E1 section S2
set load VALUE [down|up|left|right] on SEL [at FRACTION] [case NAME]   (the load there BECOMES this value: for 'change the load to 20'; add load adds another)
    e.g. set load 20 down on E1 case Q
set section NAME attribute value [attribute value ...]   (attributes: name, material, size BxH, b, h, thickness, cover, is_column, shape rectangular|circular|generic, area_override A, inertia_override I ... any attribute of the section; a circular section is shape circular with size DxD, D the diameter; a generic one is shape generic with the area (m2) and the inertia (m4))
    e.g. set section S1 size 0.3x0.6
set material NAME attribute value [attribute value ...]   (attributes: name, young 33GPa, poisson, weight, density, type concrete|steel|timber|other ...)
    e.g. set material X young 33GPa poisson 0.2

docs.title: remove
docs.text:
Deletes. An id that does not exist is an error that lists the ones that do.

remove node SEL
    e.g. remove node C
remove bar SEL
    e.g. remove bar E2
remove slab ID
    e.g. remove slab S1
remove wall ID
    e.g. remove wall W1
remove section NAME
    e.g. remove section S2
remove material NAME
    e.g. remove material X
remove support SEL
    e.g. remove support nodes y=0
remove edge REGION EDGE
    e.g. remove edge Slab 1
remove load on SEL [case NAME]
    e.g. remove load on E1 case Q
remove temperature on SEL [case NAME]
    e.g. remove temperature on E1
remove spring SEL
    e.g. remove spring B
remove case NAME
    e.g. remove case Q
remove spectrum ID
    e.g. add spectrum SP points 0 1 1 2
    e.g. remove spectrum SP
remove mass SEL [case MASSCASE]
    e.g. add analysis M mass = 1 G
    e.g. add mass B mx 2 case M
    e.g. remove mass B
remove analysis NAME
    e.g. remove analysis ULS
remove combination NAME
    e.g. remove combination C1
remove constraint ID
    e.g. remove constraint C1

docs.title: move
docs.text:
Moves nodes, to a position or by an amount.

move node SEL by DX DY | to X Y
    e.g. move node C by 0 0.5
move element SEL by DX DY | to X Y   (a bar, a slab or a wall: the id says which; `to` puts its first node, or its first corner, there)
    e.g. move element W1 by 2 0
    e.g. move element W1 to 6 1

docs.title: select and deselect
docs.text:
Mark nodes and bars in the window, as the Selection menu does. They change nothing in the model.

select nodes SEL   (marks them in the window: ids with commas, all, or a condition: select nodes x>=6)
    e.g. select nodes x>=6
select bars SEL   (marks them in the window; 'select bars y=9' is the beams at y=9, both ends)
    e.g. select bars y=9
select only nodes|bars SEL   (replaces the selection with these)
    e.g. select only bars E1
select none   (clears the selection)
    e.g. select none
select previous   (the selection before this one, as Selection > Previous selection)
    e.g. select previous
deselect nodes SEL   (takes them out of the selection)
    e.g. deselect nodes A
deselect bars SEL
    e.g. deselect bars E1
deselect all   (clears the selection)
    e.g. deselect all

docs.title: divide
docs.text:
Divides bars, triangles and quads into pieces, as the window action does. The divided id disappears: E1 becomes E1/1, E1/2, ..., so a later line cannot use it.

divide bar SEL N | size L
    e.g. divide bar E1 3
divide triangle IDS N
    e.g. divide triangle T1 2
divide quad IDS N
    e.g. divide quad Q1 2
divide element IDS N
    e.g. divide element E1 3

docs.title: copy, array, rotate, scale, mirror
docs.text:
The Edit menu as commands. A bar stands for its two nodes, a slab or wall for the nodes that define it. The copies get ids _c2, _c3, ..., and the answer lists them.

copy nodes SEL by DX DY [loads]   (also on bar, slab and wall: copy bar E1 ...; the bars, slabs and walls made of the nodes come too; with loads: their loads too)
    e.g. copy nodes A,B by 6 0
array nodes SEL rect NX DX NY DY [loads]  |  array nodes SEL circular CX CY COUNT STEP [loads]   (NX by NY copies DX, DY apart, the original being the first; COUNT copies STEP degrees apart)
    e.g. array nodes all rect 3 6 1 0
rotate nodes SEL about X Y by DEGREES [cw]   (counter-clockwise unless cw)
    e.g. rotate nodes all about 0 0 by 90
scale nodes SEL about X Y by SX [SY]
    e.g. scale nodes all about 0 0 by 2
mirror nodes SEL about X Y angle DEGREES [copy] [loads]  |  mirror nodes SEL about x=V|y=V [copy] [loads]   (the line through that point at that angle from x; without copy the nodes move)
    e.g. mirror nodes all about x=6 copy

docs.title: get
docs.text:
Reads results and facts about the model. It changes nothing; the answer is a typed value, not text to be read again.

get value QUANTITY on ID [at x=METRES | at FRACTION] [case NAME]   (one node or bar; a bar quantity needs 'at': x=2 is 2 m from the first node, 0.5 is mid-span)
    e.g. get value M on E1 at x=2 case ULS
get max QUANTITY [on SEL] [case NAME]   (the largest value and where it is)
    e.g. get max M on bars all
get min QUANTITY [on SEL] [case NAME]
    e.g. get min uy on nodes all
get absmax QUANTITY [on SEL] [case NAME]   (the largest in absolute value, with its sign)
    e.g. get absmax V on bars all
get sum QUANTITY on SEL [case NAME]   (added over nodes)
    e.g. get sum reaction fy on nodes all case Q
get diff QUANTITY NODE NODE [case NAME]   (the first minus the second)
    e.g. get diff uy B C case Q
get list QUANTITY [on SEL] [case NAME]   (at most 10 rows)
    e.g. get list reaction fy case Q
get design steel   or   timber   or   concrete columns   or   concrete bars longitudinal   or   concrete bars shear   or   concrete bars cracking   or   concrete areas x   or   concrete areas y   or   concrete areas punching   [top|bottom] [on IDS] [worst N]   (the design results already computed, worst first; it reads, it does not design. The material of the question decides: steel or timber members; concrete columns is the utilisation of the reinforced concrete columns (1.0 is the limit), with their bars and M_Rd; concrete bars longitudinal is the As of the beams and columns (top or bottom face), shear the stirrups Asw/s, cracking the crack width; concrete areas (or shells, or panels) x or y is the As of slabs and walls in that direction (top or bottom face of a slab; a wall has none), punching the punching shear. get design alone is the summary)
    e.g. get design concrete columns
    e.g. get design concrete bars longitudinal bottom worst 3
    e.g. get design concrete areas x bottom worst 1
    e.g. get design steel worst 5
get quantities   (bill of materials: element counts, lengths, areas, volume, weight and mass by material and section)
    e.g. get quantities
get topology [free_node|coincident_nodes|tee_junction|duplicate_bar|crossing]   (the model check: topology only)
    e.g. get topology
get info ID   (everything about one node, bar, section or material: where, the bars of a node; the ends, length, angle, section, hinges of a bar)
    e.g. get info E1
get modal [case NAME] [modes N]   (periods, frequencies and participating mass of a Modal case)
    e.g. get modal modes 5
get spectrum [ID] [case NAME]   (the response spectra defined in the model: points, period range, PEAK Sa, damping; with a Spectrum case, the Sa each mode picks up)
    e.g. get spectrum
get fields [NAME] [on NODES | at X Y]   (the fields defined; one of them at the nodes where it is largest, at some nodes, or at a point)
    e.g. get fields Wind at 10 6
get count nodes|bars [CONDITION]   (how many, and which: it names them; for 'the nodes with x>=7' or 'the beams at y=9': get count bars y=9; 'the nodes with no support' is get count nodes free)
    e.g. get count nodes y=0
get supports [fixed|pinned|roller]   (how many supports, and of which kinds; with a kind, how many of that kind, none included)
    e.g. get supports
get mesh triangles|quads   (how many of them in the analysed mesh)
    e.g. get mesh triangles
get distance NODE NODE   (metres)
    e.g. get distance A B
get load [fx|fy] on NODE|BAR case NAME   (a load that was applied, not a result)
    e.g. get load fy on N1 case G
get spring on NODE case NAME   (the force in a spring)
    e.g. get spring on B case LC
get coefsum   (the load combination with the largest sum of coefficients)
    e.g. get coefsum

docs.title: Where it is used
docs.text:
• Assistant: it writes the commands from your request, checks them on a copy, and applies them at once or holds them for Apply (see Creating and changing a model).
  • MCP server: the tools commands and check run them, grammar and reference give an agent the language, and get takes the same questions as the get commands (see MCP server).
  • Python: the same operations are in the engine, with names and arguments instead of text.

docs.title: Buckling lengths
docs.text: The steel (EC3 §6.3.3) and timber (EC5) member checks, and the concrete column check, need the buckling length of each physical member, not of each bar. A physical member is a chain of collinear bars, found automatically. The buckling length is L_cr = K × member length, per axis: K_y (major, in the plane), K_z (minor, out of the plane) and K_LT (lateral-torsional). In a concrete column, K_y and K_z are the effective-length factors of §5.8.

docs.title: The Buckling panel
docs.text:
Design ▸ Buckling lengths… opens the Buckling panel in the left dock:

  • The table lists the members of the current canvas selection (expanded to whole physical members), with the real length of each bar and the physical length of the member, and its K_y, K_z, K_LT, LTB and Column values. Selecting a row highlights that member on the canvas.
  • Load from selection replaces the table with the current selection; Add from selection adds more members; Load modified shows every member that already carries an override.
  • Enter K_y, K_z and K_LT (use . as the decimal separator; a blank leaves the value unchanged) and press Apply to selected or Apply to all. The values are written to every bar of the target members. Reset default (selected or all) clears the override, and the member then follows the global default.
  • LTB says whether the member is susceptible to lateral-torsional buckling (Yes, No, or — to leave it).
  • Column override (EC2 §5.8): the Is column choice (Yes, No, —) overrides, for the bars selected, the section's Physical column by default. The rest of the column data (creep ratio, bars, method) belongs to the section.

These are design-only properties: they do not change the stiffness of the model, so they can be edited on a locked model without discarding the results. Run the design again to apply them.

The model is 2D

Because the model is planar, xdfem2D cannot see the out-of-plane bracing. By default K_z uses the same member length as K_y (both default to 1.0), so the out-of-plane length equals the in-plane one unless you set K_z. Set the per-member K_z to reflect the real out-of-plane restraint.

docs.title: Free-end members (cantilevers)
docs.text:
When a physical member has a truly free end (a boundary node with nothing attached: no support, spring, other bar, triangle or constraint), xdfem2D treats it as a cantilever and applies an automatic K to K_y and K_z (a free tip is unrestrained in both planes). K_LT is left on the global default. An explicit override you set always wins. Such members are flagged with a ⚑ in the table.

It is controlled in Design ▸ Code preferences, group Buckling: free-end members (cantilevers): Auto K for a free (cantilever) end (on by default) and K for a free end (default 2.0; set, for example, 2.2 to allow for imperfect base fixity).

For timber beams that carry a beam tag, the buckling length is that of the span between supports, hinges and joining bars, and a lateral-restraint spacing you give on the beam replaces K_LT·L: see Timber.

docs.title: Design codes and preferences
docs.text: Three things set up a design before it runs: the code edition of each material, the parameters of each code, and the combinations to design for. All of them are in the Design menu.

docs.title: Code editions
docs.text:
Material Code Editions Concrete EN 1992-1-1 (EC2) 2004, 2023 Steel EN 1993-1-1 (EC3) 2005 Timber EN 1995-1-1 (EC5) 2004, 2025

The formulae are those of eurocodepy, a required dependency of xdfem2D; the application gathers the actions, calls the checks and shows the results. The report of each check names the clause it applies (see Design reports).

There are two places to choose an edition:

  • File ▸ Preferences ▸ Design sets the edition given to new models, one for each material.
  • Design ▸ Code preferences sets the edition, and every other parameter below, for the open model.

The code that a design was run with is stored inside the .x2d with its results. When you reopen a file that was already designed, its stored code takes precedence over the preference default, so a model keeps the code it was designed with. Changing any code preference discards the design results of the open model (they were computed under the old values); so does a new analysis.

What the 2023 edition changes, and what it does not

EN 1992-1-1:2023 changes the design of bars (the concrete strength fcd = ηcc·ktc·fck/γc, the shear of §8.2, the torsion of §8.3 and the combined shear and torsion), of membranes (Annex G.3), of slabs (Annex G.4) and of punching (§8.4). The crack width (EN 1992-1-1:2004 §7.3.4) and the anchorage and lap lengths keep the 2004 rules, and for columns the slenderness, second-order and N–M rules are still those of 2004; only fcd is the 2023 one. See Concrete: members, Concrete: slabs and walls and Concrete: punching.

docs.title: Code preferences
docs.text: Design ▸ Code preferences has one tab per code: EC2 · Concrete, EC3 · Steel, EC5 · Timber and General. These are all its parameters, with their defaults. A scripted model sets the same keys in the prefs of the design functions (see Python API: results and design).

docs.title: EC2: common
docs.text: Parameter Default What it is ec2_edition 2004 EN 1992-1-1:2004 or :2023 gamma_c 1.5 partial factor of concrete alpha_cc 1.0 long-term factor αcc (2004). In 2023, ηcc·ktc is used instead gamma_s 1.15 partial factor of reinforcement

docs.title: EC2: serviceability (crack width)
docs.text: Parameter Default What it is wk_max 0.3 mm crack-width limit sls_combo Quasi-permanent the SLS combination: Quasi-permanent, Frequent or Characteristic

docs.title: EC2: beam bars (areas to bars)
docs.text:
How the required areas of a beam become bars. See Concrete: members.

Parameter Default What it is beam_diameters 10, 12, 16, 20, 25, 32 mm bar diameters available beam_stirrup_mm 8 mm stirrup diameter assumed for the cover beam_max_layers 2 maximum layers per face beam_max_diameters 2 maximum distinct diameters per face of a beam beam_n_through 2 continuous (through) bars per face beam_symmetry rule bar symmetry: rule (odd counts of 3 or more allowed, symmetric curtailment), even (even counts only) or none beam_zone_mode cutoff zones along each span: cutoff (at the steps of the envelope) or fixed (fractions of the span) beam_cutoff_levels 3 steps of the envelope, in cutoff mode beam_min_zone_length 0.5 m shorter zones are merged beam_support_bottom_ratio 0.25 bottom steel that reaches the supports, as a fraction of the maximum span steel (EC2 9.2.1.4) beam_shift_d 0 shift of the envelope, in effective depths (EC2 9.2.1.3); 0 is off beam_top_min_ratio 0 As,min imposed on the top face, as a fraction of As,min beam_stirrup_legs 2 stirrup legs beam_stirrup_diameters 6, 8, 10, 12 mm stirrup diameters available beam_stirrup_spacings 75 … 300 mm stirrup spacings available beam_anchorage_shape straight bar ends: straight or bent (hooks) beam_lap_percentage 50 % lapped bars in a section (ρ1) beam_bar_length 12 m commercial bar length

docs.title: EC2:2023: punching
docs.text: Parameter Default What it is gamma_v 1.4 partial factor of punching eta_sys 1.5 system factor of punching dmax 20 mm maximum aggregate size

docs.title: EC2:2023: concrete strength and membranes
docs.text: Parameter Default What it is ec2_k_tc 1.0 ktc: 1.00 for a concrete loaded three months or more after casting, 0.85 otherwise ec2_nu_mode simple ν of membranes and of the sandwich layers (Annex G): simple is 0.4 (Eq. G.8), strain is from the strains (Eq. G.9) ec2_strut_model annex_f the concrete strut of membranes and, in 2004, of Wood–Armer slabs: annex_f is ν·fcd with ν = 0.6(1 − fck/250), 6.109 is EN 1992-2 §6.109 (with the angle to the elastic direction) ec2_slab_method auto slabs, Annex G.4: auto uses Tables G.2/G.3 and the sandwich model where they do not apply, optimum only the tables, sandwich only the sandwich model

docs.title: EC3: steel
docs.text: Parameter Default What it is ec3_edition 2005 EN 1993-1-1:2005 gamma_M0 1.0 cross-sections gamma_M1 1.0 member buckling gamma_M2 1.25 fracture and joints steel_class4_effective on use the effective properties of Class 4 sections steel_ltb_rolled on the rolled and welded sections method for lateral-torsional buckling (§6.3.2.3) steel_interaction_method B interaction factors kij (§6.3.3): Annex B (method 2) or Annex A (method 1) steel_ky, steel_kz, steel_klt 1.0 default buckling-length factors, per axis and for lateral-torsional buckling steel_E, steel_G 210000, 81000 MPa moduli steel_cmy, steel_cmz, steel_cmlt 0.9 default equivalent-moment factors steel_c1 1.0 default LTB moment factor

docs.title: EC5: timber
docs.text: Parameter Default What it is ec5_edition 2004 EN 1995-1-1:2004 or :2025 timber_gammaM_solid 1.3 γM of solid timber (C, D) timber_gammaM_glulam 1.25 γM of glued laminated timber (GL) timber_gammaM_lvl 1.2 γM of LVL timber_gammaM_clt 1.25 γM of CLT timber_gammaM_panels 1.2 γM of wood panels (plywood, OSB) timber_taper_step_warn 0.1 warn when the depth of a tapered beam jumps by more than this between bars

docs.title: Buckling: free-end members
docs.text:
Parameter Default What it is cantilever_auto on apply an automatic K to a member with a free end cantilever_k 2.0 that K, for K_y and K_z

See Buckling lengths.

docs.title: Other
docs.text: A national annex is chosen in a script with the ec2_annex preference (a country code; none by default). It is not in the dialog. The strengths fck, fyk and fy are not preferences: they come from the material of each section (see Materials and sections for design).

docs.title: Design combinations
docs.text:
Design ▸ Design combinations chooses which load combinations are checked, in two tabs: ULS (all the designs) and SLS (the crack width). Every combination of the model is listed in both, and a combination can be in only one of them: ticking it in one tab clears it in the other. When nothing has been chosen yet, the ids that start with ULS or ELU are ticked for ULS and those that start with SLS or ELS for SLS.

Generate the EN 1990 combinations with Analysis ▸ Auto Comb. (EN1990)… (Ctrl+Shift+C) (they take the action type of each load case, and the ψ factors, which have defaults from eurocodepy), or define your own on the Combinations sub-tab. See Analysis.

docs.title: Concrete: slabs and walls
docs.text:
The reinforced-concrete design of area elements (triangles and quads whose section is of type Concrete) to EN 1992-1-1, with Design ▸ Concrete areas (ULS). What it designs depends on the domain:

Domain The elements are What is designed Plane walls and panels (membranes) the reinforcement in two orthogonal directions, from the in-plane forces, with a check of the concrete strut Plate slabs the bending reinforcement of the bottom and top layers in two directions, and the reinforcement for the out-of-plane shear

Punching, which is a check at the columns of a slab, is on Concrete: punching. The materials and covers are on Materials and sections for design, and the parameters of this page on Design codes and preferences.

The combinations must be plain. The design needs the stresses or moments of each element, and an envelope combination (an envelope, a seismic one) stores only displacement bands, so it carries none. Select at least one non-envelope combination in Design ▸ Design combinations; the message of the design says so when none works, and names the sections whose material has no usable fck or fyk.

docs.title: Walls and panels (plane model)
docs.text:
Each triangle or quad is a membrane, so the design works from the forces per unit length, n_xx = σx·t, n_yy = σy·t and n_xy = τxy·t [kN/m] (t is the thickness), with the Wood and Baumann membrane equations of eurocodepy. For each direction the steel area is As = force/fyd, and the force is split evenly between a top and a bottom layer, as orthogonal wall and slab reinforcement is usually detailed.

The concrete strut is checked as well, and a crushed strut cannot be cured with more steel:

  • EN 1992-1-1:2004 (Annex F): the compression σc is compared with ν·fcd, with ν = 0.6(1 − fck/250), and with fcd only where no reinforcement is required (biaxial compression). The preference ec2_strut_model = 6.109 uses instead the strength of EN 1992-2 §6.109 (with the angle between the strut and the elastic principal direction).
  • EN 1992-1-1:2023 (Annex G.3, Table G.1): σcd ≤ ν·fcd, with ν = 0.4 (ec2_nu_mode = simple, Eq. G.8) or from the strains (Eq. G.9), and fcd = ηcc·ktc·fck/γc.

Each row carries the ν used, the limit ν·fcd that σc is compared with, the edition, and θ (cot θ), which is undefined where no reinforcement is required.

docs.title: EN 1992-1-1:2004
docs.text:
The element moments are turned into the Wood–Armer design moments m*x,bot, m*y,bot, m*x,top and m*y,top [kNm/m]. Each of the four reinforcements (bottom and top, x and y) is designed as a strip 1 m wide with the flexure of EC2, with its own effective depth d = t − cover taken from the covers of the section for that face and direction, and the minimum slab reinforcement of §9.3.1.1 is applied to each tensioned direction.

The Wood–Armer design has no strut check in the text of the Eurocode. Where the strut of the sandwich layers would exceed ν·fcd, the row carries a note and strut_warning is set.
